result: HDX-MS reveals that Ric-8A binding induces extensive structural changes in Gαi1, including deprotection of the nucleotide-binding scaffold (P-loop, β5-αG loop, β-sheet elements β1, β4, β5, and α-helical elements αG and α4) and destabilization of the Ras domain-helical domain interface (αF, α5, α1), disrupting secondary structure that supports the nucleotide-binding site and facilitating domain separation.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly state 'the data are of high quality and support the conclusions' and describe the work as showing 'broad increases in flexibility across more of the Ras-like domain upon complex formation (a loosening of the tertiary structure).' The reviewers affirm that the study demonstrates Ric-8A 'stabilizes a poorly ordered nucleotide G protein subunit (consistent with chaperone function)' and note the findings are 'novel and fascinating.'

result: HDX-MS data indicate that Ric-8A forms a broad interaction surface with Gαi1 that includes the C-terminus (strongly protected), Switch I and Switch II (modestly protected), and structural elements of the helical domain near the Ras domain interface, with the C-terminus likely making the most intimate contacts.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly affirm this finding, stating 'Ric-8A shares some key properties with GPCRs in how they interact with G-α, in that the C-terminal helix of the G protein is likely a key interaction site' and 'interactions also appear to be formed between Ric-8A and two of the switch regions of the α subunit.' They note 'the data are of high quality and support the conclusions.'

result: HDX-MS identifies a C-terminal region of Ric-8A (residues 454-470) that becomes highly protected (25% decrease in deuteration) upon Gαi1 binding, and alanine scanning mutagenesis reveals specific residues (V455A, T456A, R458A, P466A, G469A) and truncation (1-452) that significantly impair GEF activity, demonstrating this region contributes substantially to Ric-8A GEF activity.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly state 'The authors go on to show that a region predicted to be disordered at the C-terminus of Ric-8A is highly protected from exchange upon complex formation. The authors hypothesize that this is an important G protein binding site, an idea they support via site-directed mutagenesis and truncation. These Ric-8A variants display significantly reduced nucleotide exchange on Gαi.' They affirm 'the data are of high quality and support the conclusions.'

result: HDX-MS shows that changes induced by Ric-8A are largely reversed upon GTP binding, with the P-loop and α1 becoming moderately protected (opposite to Ric-8A-bound state), and Switch II and the C-terminus of β3 also showing protection, consistent with structural rigidification induced by GTP binding.
evaluation: Reviewers do not explicitly critique these findings and state 'the data are of high quality and support the conclusions.' The comparison between GDP, Ric-8A-bound, and GTP-bound states is central to the manuscript's argument about reversibility of conformational changes, which reviewers accept.

result: Comparison of HDX data suggests that Ric-8A and GPCRs adopt different strategies to induce structural transitions in Gα that facilitate nucleotide exchange, with the extent of structural perturbation induced by Ric-8A being at least comparable to, and possibly more extensive than, that induced by β2AR on Gαs.
evaluation: Reviewers request that the authors 'soften their tone slightly on the role of the C-terminus and the 5-6 loop on nucleotide exchange' in light of recent structural data (Carpenter et al., Nature, 2016) and suggest discussing NMR results showing partially unfolded states. They note 'the β2AR-Gs complex study seems like a bit of an outlier in how little unfolding there is' and question whether there is 'a spectrum of relative unfolding given the identity of the GEF and the α subunit.' This indicates uncertainty about the comparative interpretation.

result: Computational modeling using Robetta predicts that Ric-8A adopts an armadillo fold similar to β-catenin, with the C-terminal ~130 residues and N-terminal 400 residues constituting distinct structural domains.
evaluation: Reviewers express 'one minor concern is the validity of the Ric-8A model – can this be validated by CD or other biophysical measures?' This indicates uncertainty about the computational model's reliability, though they acknowledge it is consistent with prior sequence analysis. They note this is a 'weakness of this work' because 'there is no atomic structure of Ric-8A.'

result: The manuscript states there is no direct evidence that Ric-8A is a physiological GEF and that whether Ric-8 isoforms have dual functions as both chaperones and GEFs has not been resolved.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly agree with this assessment, stating 'It is not really clear whether Ric8 is a physiological GEF of G-αs or whether they serve only as chaperones. While there is cellular evidence of the latter there really isn't any satisfying evidence of the former. Therefore, it is suggested that Ric8 might really be referred to as having or displaying GEF activity but not necessarily be referred to as a GEF, or a physiologically relevant GEF.'

result: Ric-8A binding does not induce striking changes in slow protein dynamics as measured by the slope of HDX with time.
evaluation: Reviewers raise concerns about interpretation of HDX kinetics, asking 'Could an attempt be made to distinguish the deuterium exchange on G-α from the ric8 protein-protein interaction from the difference in exchange rates simply because the G protein is nucleotide-free.' They question 'whether Ric8 truly stabilizes the 'open' conformation of the Gα, or simply the nucleotide-free form, which happens to be in the 'open' conformation.' This suggests uncertainty about what the HDX kinetics data actually reveal.

result: The HDX-MS experimental methodology achieved complete coverage of Gαi1 and 87% coverage of Ric-8A, with the Gαi1:Ric-8A complex remaining intact and active throughout the experiment.
evaluation: Reviewers state 'the work is of high technical quality' and 'the experimental design is rigorous. The data are of high quality.' They request that supplemental figures showing primary data be moved to main figures, indicating they value the experimental data quality but want better presentation.
